source.basis: Operator spec page; structured facts only, no operator prose reproduced.

reading.body:
CyrusOne's Totowa NJ campus publishes 6 MW of IT capacity and 200,000 square feet of technical space, and nothing about how that power is delivered to racks.

The gap matters because the same 6 MW supports very different buildings. At 40 kW per rack, a common AI training density, it is roughly 150 racks. At 10 kW per rack it is about 600. The operator publishes no rack count, no accelerator count, and no power density, so the conversion is the reader's, not the operator's. Nothing in the data describes electrical topology, cooling method, or on-site generation, which are the things that decide whether a hall can hold dense training hardware.

The only certification listed is SSAE 16 Type II, which covers controls over financial reporting rather than power or cooling. No tenant is named. The campus scores 52 on a weighted mean of published IT capacity and operator type, with announced expansion listed as missing, so the score reflects what is published rather than what the building can do.

New Jersey has 48 mapped facilities, and only five publish any capacity figure. Those five total 111.3 MW, of which this campus is 6 MW, about five percent, ranking it fourth in the state. That 111.3 MW is a floor on New Jersey data center load, not a measure of it, because most facilities in the state publish no number at all.

suitability.basis: weighted mean of the published inputs named here, scaled to 100; formula on the methodology page
